thread:
Samir (Docs): heads-up: opened a small PR to clarify the quota dashboard metric labels and an example for the metering header usage. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/452 :mag:
Leah (Eng): looks good at a glance. what's the exact metric name we're surfacing from runtime? is it 'redwood.tokens' or 'redwood.token_count'? we should match the dashboard query to the ingestion field.
Mike (Billing): it's 'redwood.token_count' in the ingestion pipeline right now. historical data had a 'tokens' alias for a few weeks during the migration, which is why some panels show double counts. we should add a note for the migration window.
Samir (Docs): thanks — i'll update the docs PR to show the canonical field name and include a short 'migration note' block. also adding an SDK snippet example for how to send the metering header.
Zara (Analytics): FYI the dashboard panels also expect the unit to be 'token-seconds' for burst calculations, but the pricing math uses flat tokens. can we add a small clarifying sentence in the pricing doc to avoid confusion? :thinking:
Samir (Docs): sure. draft change: "Dashboard panels show token-seconds for burst-normalized visualization; billing units are plain tokens. For cost calculations, use token_count aggregated over the billing window." will that work?
Mike (Billing): yes — that language is accurate. please also add an explicit example with numbers so folks can see the math.
Samir (Docs): adding example: 
```
# Example billing math
period_tokens = 1_200_000  # sum of token_count over month
price_per_1k = 0.12  # $ per 1k tokens
cost = (period_tokens / 1000) * price_per_1k
# => (1200000 / 1000) * 0.12 = $144
```
will put that under 'Pricing examples'.
Leah (Eng): quick technical note: the runtime will sometimes emit the header as `x-redwood-usage: tokens=1234; model=\"rw-1.0\"`. docs should show a JSON SDK snippet and also the raw header example so infra folks can debug.
Samir (Docs): good call. i'll add both. proposed SDK snippet (python):
```python
headers = {"x-redwood-usage": "tokens=1234; model=\"rw-1.0\""}
resp = client.generate(prompt, headers=headers)
```
Samir (Docs): also adding a short migration note: "If you see doubled counts in panels between 2024-11-10 and 2024-11-17, that's the old alias overlap; use the canonical `redwood.token_count` for billing and `token-seconds` only for burst charts."
Zara (Analytics): for the docs query examples, can you include the exact PromQL we use for the panel? saves a roundtrip. e.g.:
```promql
sum(rate(redwood_token_count_total[5m])) by (model, customer_id)
```
That would help reproducing the chart.
Samir (Docs): will paste that into the dashboard section. one more question: do we need a note about the embedding-only endpoints counting as tokens or as embeddings units? some customers ask about this distinction.
Mike (Billing): embeddings are metered separately (embedding_units). please add a single-line note: "Embeddings endpoints are billed in embedding_units; text generation uses token_count." should include link to pricing table.
Samir (Docs): done in branch. tagging @Leah and @Zara for quick technical review, and @Mike for pricing ack. PTAL when you have 20m. :pray:
Leah (Eng): reading now. small nit: change header sample to use lower-case `x-redwood-usage` consistently and include semicolon spacing example. otherwise lgtm.
Zara (Analytics): lgtm, added the PromQL line and adjusted the chart description to mention the 5m window and the burst normalization.
Mike (Billing): acked the pricing example and migration note. tiny wording suggestion: change "billing window" to "billing period" for consistency with invoices.
Samir (Docs): updated per all suggestions, pushed a new commit. anyone object to merging after CI passes?
Leah (Eng): no objections. will do a quick look after CI.

Samir (Docs): merged. thanks everyone! i'll follow up with a small note in the release changelog and ping customer-success about the migration window.
Zara (Analytics): thanks — i'll update the internal dashboard runbook to mention the alias window and add a check for double-count spikes.
Mike (Billing): thanks all :thumbsup:
Samir (Docs): closing thread after release note goes out.
